Subject: Post-discovery: next steps & proposed rotating demo windows

Hi Emily / Carlos —

Thanks again for a productive call today. Quick recap from our side:
- Goal: evaluate Redwood Inference as the inference runtime for your patient-facing summarization pipeline (low-latency SLOs, predictable cost, and on-prem/private deployment options for PHI).
- Key stakeholders: Emily (CTO), Carlos (Platform Lead), + 2 engineering leads who will join the technical deep-dive.
- Main constraints: Aurora needs at least one demo window per week that is friendly to both US and EU engineering participants; some execs prefer a rotating pattern so the burden of evening calls isn't always on the same region.

Next steps we discussed:
1) 60–75 minute technical deep-dive (model selection, latency profiling, privacy controls) — invite to engineering stakeholders.
2) Share a short mutual action plan (attached) and a proposed rotating schedule so all teams can coordinate.

Proposed rotating pattern (three-week rotation) — times shown with common conversions:
- Slot A (US-friendly): Tue 08:30–09:45 PT / Tue 11:30–12:45 ET / Tue 16:30–17:45 UTC
- Slot B (EU-friendly): Wed 09:00–10:15 CET / Wed 08:00–09:15 UTC / Wed 03:00–04:15 PT
- Slot C (APAC-friendly): Thu 10:00–11:15 SGT / Thu 03:00–04:15 UTC / Wed 22:00–23:15 PT

Pattern idea: Week 1 use Slot A, Week 2 Slot B, Week 3 Slot C, then repeat. That gives Aurora predictable windows and spreads the evening burden across regions. If that cadence works, we can lock recurring invites and share a single calendar with rotating labels.

Attachments: I attached a short mutual action plan (MA_plan_Aurora.xlsx) and our product brief. Also dropping our HubSpot deal link and a draft calendar matrix in Drive.

Can you confirm: (a) whether the 3-week rotation sounds reasonable, and (b) which of the next two weeks you'd prefer for the first technical deep-dive? I can send calendar invites once you pick a slot.

Thanks — looking forward.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
